{{Navbar-GOGPT-tracker}}
'''Dedisa power station''' is an operating power station of at least 335-megawatts (MW) in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape, South Africa.

==Background==

It is currently operating on diesel but was built with the intention to convert to natural gas and Combined Cycle technology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hulisani.co.za/project/avon-and-dedisa-peaking-power|title=Avon and Dedisa Peaking Power Investment {{!}} Hulisani Investment Opportunity {{!}} SA|last=Hulisani|date=2019-09-01|website=Hulisani|language=en-US|access-date=2022-06-20}}</ref><ref name=":0">http://www.energy.gov.za/IRP/2019/IRP-2019.pdf</ref>

Dedisa power station and [[Avon Power Station,]] have a combined capacity of 1005 MW and are privately-owned. Dedisa started operations in September 2015 after a 24-month construction period.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peakers.com/dedisa.html|title=Avon Dedisa Peaking Power Dedisa Peaking Power|website=www.peakers.com|access-date=2022-06-20}}</ref>

It solely supplies power to Eskom under a 15-year Power Purchase Agreement (PPA).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peakers.com/dedisa.html|title=Avon Dedisa Peaking Power Dedisa Peaking Power|website=www.peakers.com|access-date=2022-06-20}}</ref>
